title: `{Dedicated,Shared}WorkerGlobalScope` instances should be immutable prototype exotic objects
body:
Currently, HTML specifies that `WindowProxy` instances have a special [`[[SetPrototypeOf]]`](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#windowproxy-setprototypeof) internal method that defers to TC39's [`SetImmutablePrototype`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-set-immutable-prototype) abstract operation. WebIDL also defines (["create an interface prototype object" algorithm](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#create-an-interface-prototype-object), step 8) that any interface prototype objects whose interfaces either have the `[Global]` extended attribute or have a subclass with that attribute, are [immutable prototype exotic objects](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-immutable-prototype-exotic-objects), which also override their `[[SetPrototypeOf]]` internal method in the same way.

This was meant so you couldn't switch a prototype in `window`'s prototype chain for an unrelated object. This was issue #1235.

However, the WebIDL spec applies this to any interface prototype object that is a (non-strict) superclass of a global interface. This includes the global object prototype chain for workers. But HTML does not specify that the prototype of `{Dedicated,Shared}WorkerGlobalScope` *instances* cannot change.

The WPT test for this, [`webidl/ecmascript-binding/global-immutable-prototype.any.js`](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/webidl/ecmascript-binding/global-immutable-prototype.any.js), tests that changing the global object's prototype fails *for both windows and workers*. And [all browsers pass this test for dedicated workers](https://wpt.fyi/results/webidl/ecmascript-binding/global-immutable-prototype.any.worker.html). WebKit [fails the test for shared workers](https://wpt.fyi/results/webidl/ecmascript-binding/global-immutable-prototype.any.sharedworker.html), but not because `self`'s prototype can be changed, but because *`SharedWorkerGlobalScope.prototype`*'s prototype can be changed.

Therefore, it seems like the global objects for dedicated and shared workers should also be immutable prototype exotic objects, for consistency at least. (I don't think I can speak about the security reasons that led to #1235 in the first place.)
